issue_reference: Assigned in the registration pull request rather than guessed in advance.
hypothesis: The opponent-mixture comparison found that the hard line-up fails all three retention gates and the mixed line-up passes all three, with no measurable difference between them. The dose-response then confounded that reading. Every one of its arms trained against the hard line-up, and its middle dose passed all three retention gates at the same budget, so the mixture comparison had measured the line-up at a learning rate where the hard line-up loses capability whatever it trains against. Retention is governed by the rate, and whether the line-up matters at all once the rate is right is open again. This comparison settles it by varying the line-up alone at the dose the ladder selected, at six times the budget both earlier readings were taken at, retaining the trajectory so the answer can be read along it rather than only at its end.

prior_evidence.trainable_scope: Lifting the Task 3 freeze beat the frozen regime by 1.429 score with the interval [0.888, 1.996], and training under the frozen scope was itself significantly worse than not training at all. Every arm here therefore registers the all_weights scope and the frozen regime is not carried.
prior_evidence.opponent_mixture: At 400 episodes and learning rate 0.0005 the hard line-up failed all three retention gates and the mixed line-up passed all three, with no measurable tournament difference between them.
prior_evidence.finetune_dose: The learning-rate ladder was run entirely against the hard line-up. Its middle dose, 0.0002, beat the unchanged incumbent on score by 0.708 with the interval [0.175, 1.279] and passed all three retention gates; the largest dose lost two of them and the smallest lost all three while gaining least. That dose is registered here for every arm, and it is also what reopens the line-up question: the mixture comparison measured the line-up at a rate where the hard line-up fails retention regardless.
prior_evidence.power: The unchanged incumbent scored 2.350, 2.200 and 1.375 on three independent forty-world sets, a spread of about one point of score for an agent that did not change. No absolute score is comparable across comparisons, and any earlier claim of smaller world-set noise is superseded by this. Contrasts within a comparison are paired on shared worlds and are unaffected, which is why every conclusion drawn here is a paired contrast.

intervention.baseline_shared_by_every_arm: the installed Task 3 incumbent as the starting point, the all_weights trainable scope, native rewards with no approach shaping, one optimizer update per eligible transition and learning rate 0.0002
intervention.persistence: training-only; evaluation loads the unchanged archived agent
intervention.methodology_change: This pair runs under a changed experiment setup, registered here so the change is visible before any results exist. Earlier comparisons spent their budget on breadth - more arms and replicas at 400 episodes each - and kept only the final checkpoint, which assumes training improves monotonically and cannot recover a peak that decays before the end. These spend it on depth: fewer replicas, several times the episodes, and the trajectory retained at registered milestones so it can be evaluated where it was rather than only where it stopped. Training is sequential, so the milestone at episode N is exactly the agent N episodes would have produced from the same seeds; a budget question therefore needs one long run read along its trajectory, not one run per budget. Progress writes are durable and a killed replica resumes from minutes ago instead of from episode zero, which is what makes a run of this length survivable. The purpose shifts with the setup: these are rehearsals for a long training run, powered to describe a trajectory rather than to establish a small difference between arms.
intervention.registered_risk: The retained milestones are not evaluated by this run. They are written so the trajectory can be evaluated afterwards; the gates below are decided on the final checkpoints alone, exactly as the completed comparisons were.

random_episode_schedule: Per arm: for each block of `random_episode_period` episodes, random.Random(agent_seed + 168000000 + block_index).randrange(period) selects one fully random episode and the rest are greedy. A period of five reproduces the registered #168 schedule exactly, including its seed stream.
primary_endpoint: Mean native score per game on classic-rule-based against the unchanged incumbent. Tournament placing is decided by score.

uncertainty.method: hierarchical paired bootstrap over replicas and shared worlds
uncertainty.family: one test family per treatment arm that can be promoted; the promotion rule is conjunctive, so only the arm count is Bonferroni-adjusted
uncertainty.role: registered decision input, not a post-hoc description

selection: An arm is promotable only if every applicable integrity gate, every retention gate and every efficacy gate passes. Among promotable arms the largest mean score gain over the unchanged incumbent is chosen, and within it the median-final replica by that score. The best-looking replica is not selectable. If no arm is promotable the installed incumbent remains the submission candidate.
scientific_gates: Original cumulative Task 1/2/3 requirements are unchanged; this exploratory comparison cannot retrospectively establish any of them.
known_gate_defect: The frozen_online_weights gate is reported as not applicable here, because every arm registers the scope whose purpose is to move those weights. The invalid-action gate compares each trained artifact against the unchanged reference rather than demanding a global zero it could never reach.

machine_allocation.training: 5 concurrent workers, one torch thread each
machine_allocation.latency: one worker on an otherwise idle machine; the only latency source

authorization: Owner 1BlauNitrox authorized one registered comparison per host on 15 September 2026, to run unattended overnight ahead of the long training run. No automatic extension, no automatic promotion; the README follows completed results.
